subject: POC scope, KPIs and environment readiness for HelioHealth trial
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — HelioHealth POC scope and immediate asks

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and the immediate asks so we can get your POC scheduled next week: 

Scope we agreed:
- Short proof-of-concept (3 weeks) to validate integration and production economics for your clinical-document summarization flow.
- Primary evaluation axes: latency (p95), throughput (concurrent request shape), cost/token, and quality against your clinical QA rubric.

Immediate asks from HelioHealth:
1) Sample workload (50–100 representative documents + 500 labelled QA pairs) that we can ingest into a sandbox.
2) Network details for outbound firewall rules and any egress restrictions (IP allowlist vs private peering).
3) Your procurement contact so we can start a simple MSA/PO path in parallel.

Attachments: helio_poc_requirements.xlsx (I attached a short checklist), security questionnaire (please see the stub we filled) — we will follow-up with any clarifying Qs.

Proposed next steps:
- We confirm the kickoff and test window by EOD Monday (2027-07-19).
- Redwood will provide a draft POC playbook and an initial KPI slate for you to review (I’ve attached a draft playbook: redwood_poc_playbook.pdf).

Owner on our side: Rafael (AM lead) + Ben (solutions/ops) + Monica (success).

If that aligns, I’ll publish the kickoff invite and hand over to Ben for environment/workload specifics.

Thanks — Rafael

--

- Procurement (cc’d) needs an estimated SOW and a cost outline for a short-term POC — can you send a simple one-page estimate + any standard terms?

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — POC kickoff proposal and initial KPI slate

Sara — great to meet you on the call. I’ll own the environment setup and the evaluation plan. Proposed kickoff and evaluation approach below: 

Kickoff: 2027-07-26 (work window: 2027-07-26 to 2027-08-15) — flexible if you need a different start.

Initial KPI slate (draft):
- Latency: p95 response time target: 250 ms (with a secondary agreed threshold at 350 ms during cold-start windows).
- Throughput: sustain 30 req/s steady-state and support 100 req/s burst for short windows; 99th percentile of request success under load.
- Cost: target cost/token < $0.0006 (we’ll run token estimates on your sample workload and provide a cost projection).
- Quality: human-evaluated accuracy (clinical extraction/summary alignment) >= 85% on your QA rubric and automated metric delta vs baseline <= 10% degradation.

Evaluation plan:
1) Baseline run: run current internal model/heuristic and capture metrics.
2) Redwood-run: run two variants (small fast model + medium quality model) against same sample set.
3) Instrumentation: we’ll provide a short instrumentation guide (endpoint, headers, token logging).
4) Two checkpoints: mid-POC readout (1 week in) and final readout (EOW).

Operational asks for HelioHealth:
- Confirm sample data delivery dates and preferred connectivity (IP allowlist vs private peering).
- Provide a point of contact for procurement and network.

I’ll drop a shared folder with scripts and an initial load generator. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_helio-poc-materials

If that looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff and pre-kickoff tech huddle.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Trials | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0144
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@heliohealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: POC playbook: owners, measurement plan, and acceptance gates

Sara / team — I expanded the draft playbook into concrete acceptance gates and assigned owners so we can move quickly once data and network details arrive. Key points below: 

Owners: 
- Redwood AM (Rafael) — commercial lead, cadence owner.
- Solutions (Ben) — sandbox environment, load tests, token modeling.
- Customer Success (Monica) — final evaluation, human review coordination, rollout plan.

Acceptance gates (must be met for POC to be considered successful):
1) Functional: 95% of test prompts produce syntactically correct summaries (no truncation/errors).
2) Latency: p95 < 250 ms for the chosen model under steady-state test; if sustained breach >350 ms we flag as fail.
3) Throughput: sustain 30 req/s steady-state for 30+ minutes during load test with <1% error rate.
4) Cost: modeled cost/token projection with running token sample shows projected monthly unit cost <= target ($0.0006/token); we’ll provide ongoing cost telemetry.
5) Quality: Minimum pass = 85% human-verified agreement on 200-sample QA subset; secondary metric using automated F1 against labelled set (threshold >= 0.7).

Test methodology and timing:
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): data transfer, IP allowlist, sandbox access.
- Week 1: baseline and Redwood small-model run + mid-POC readout (metrics and examples).
- Week 2: medium-model run, stress tests, cost modeling, human QC.
- Final readout: consolidated metrics, sample outputs, and recommended model for production.

Model variants: we recommend starting with redwood-3b-qa for latency/cost parity; run redwood-13b for a quality comparison if the initial pass looks promising. Please let us know which you prefer to start with.

Open items for HelioHealth: dataset drop date, procurement contact + PO timeline, and confirmation of the model variant.

I’ll update the playbook artifact in the Drive and attach the latest PDF (redwood_poc_playbook.pdf).

Thanks — Monica

--
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (212) 555-0177
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@heliohealth.com>

Date: 2027-07-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC playbook: owners, measurement plan, and acceptance gates

Thanks — this is very clear and actionable. Quick confirmations from our side: 
- We will provide the first dataset tranche by 2027-07-23 and final by 2027-07-26.
- Procurement will aim to provide a PO by 2027-07-29 (procurement contact cc’d here).
- For the POC start, we prefer to begin with redwood-3b-qa to validate latency/cost; if quality gaps appear we’ll run the 13b comparison.
- Small tweak to latency target: we expect p95 <= 300 ms as acceptable for our initial environment given upstream network variability. If you can capture both 250 ms and 300 ms bands in the readouts that will be helpful.

Please send the kickoff invites and the pre-kickoff tech huddle time slots. Looking forward to the trial.

Sara
